config_name: iPad Air 13-inch — M4 8-core CPU / 9-core GPU, 12GB RAM, 128GB SSD, 13" Liquid Retina + Magic Keyboard

specs.display_type: Liquid Retina IPS LCD (fully laminated, anti-reflective, no ProMotion)
specs.ports: 1x USB-C (USB 3 10Gb/s, DisplayPort), magnetic Magic Keyboard connector, Smart Connector
specs.keyboard_notes: Magic Keyboard for iPad Air 13" included in price: scissor keys with full function row (unlit), glass trackpad, cantilever hinge
specs.pen_support: Apple Pencil Pro +$168.99 (BBY sale; ~$199 Apple) — not included in total; Pencil USB-C +$99; hover supported

battery.notes: 36.59Wh cell. Apple claims 10h web/video Wi-Fi (9h cellular); users report ~8-8.5h mixed real-world use.

price.notes: Tablet-only $1,299.00 (apple.com/ca, verified 2026-11-24) + Magic Keyboard Air 13" $399.99 (BBY 19204078). Cellular variant +$200 ($1,499 tablet). Pencil Pro not included.

reviews.quote: The fiercest competitor for the iPad Pro is home-made. Pros: brute top performance, WiFi very fast, high-quality unibody chassis, USB-C with 10 GBit/s, two external displays possible, good color accuracy (PWM-free), well-balanced speakers, high recycled content. Cons: slow 60 Hz display, battery charging takes time, SoC throttles under sustained load. (NBC review of the iPad Air 13" M4 2026; 11" shares SoC and chassis design.)

praises: Cheapest way into the 13" M4 Air — same chip, 12GB RAM and chassis as every pricier tier (r/ipad)
13" at 616g/6.1mm: the biggest usable canvas per gram of anything Apple sells
Air Magic Keyboard function row + glass trackpad make it a genuine laptop substitute for docs/email
Fanless silence with M4 burst performance that outruns most $1,700 ultrabooks in short tasks
Wi-Fi 7 and 6K@60 external display support future-proof the connection story
complaints: 128GB is tight on a $1,300 tablet — users report it filling with one season of downloads plus a few pro apps
60Hz panel: no ProMotion at this price is the line's most repeated complaint
LCD blacks look grey in dark rooms vs any OLED
iPadOS desktop-app parity gap (no Xcode/full Excel macros) regardless of chip

design_philosophy: The Air line sells near-Pro hardware at a deliberate-cut price: M4-class speed, Pro chassis language, full accessory ecosystem — paid for with a 60Hz laminated LCD and USB-C 10Gb/s. This entry tier is the line's price-anchor: identical silicon to the top configs, with storage as the only sacrifice.
rating_notes: Pro score attached from NBC review of the iPad Air 13" M4 2026 (87%, gap-fill 2026-11-24). Ratings inferred from the 13" M4 256GB line anchor (SHARED-ipad-air.md): identical silicon/display; creative_work −0.3 for 128GB scratch/headroom friction. No verbatim pro score found (bot-walls) — disclosed, none invented. Ecosystem 6.5 per tablets-file rule. Battery on ~8.3h real use. Upgradability 1.0: soldered everything; 128GB makes external USB-C SSD storage a near-requirement for media users. Image URL is BBY CDN best guess (closest-SKU image).
standouts: Lowest-cost 13" M4 Air bundle with keyboard included
Same 12GB RAM and M4 as all pricier tiers — no performance tax at the entry tier
dealbreakers: 128GB is uncomfortable for anyone shooting 4K video or installing several pro apps
